plates.title: The Spine of the Argument
plates.prompt: An illuminated manuscript page, vertical 2:3, aged parchment colour with faded gold leaf accents, brown ink linework, soft blues and ochres for shading, in the hand of a medieval naturalist's bestiary. Down the center runs a thin vine-like line connecting twelve roundels in a single descending spine, each roundel a small framed scene: at top, a scribe-naturalist peers through wires into a glowing tissue slice (NEW EYES ON THE BRAIN); below it two mirrored overlapping circles glow together (SHARED PATTERN) beside an arrow of light passing neuron to neuron (DIRECTED FLOW); next a puzzled neuron-figure stands where two streams converge without resolving (FLOW ALONE FALLS SHORT); then an ornate cartouche redrawing FIGURE A as an illuminated diagram — a great oval holding two overlapping circles, shaded regions distinguishing their parts, no lettering (SPLITTING THE WHOLE); then twelve hooded council-figures holding differing measuring rods around an empty throne (NO ONE TRUE MEASURE); then a dense needle-grid pressed into a glowing tissue slice (THE RECORDING ARRAY). Below this the spine forks into a cluster of three roundels side by side — a bright haloed cluster of neurons radiating light amid dimmer ones (THE RICH CLUB GLOWS), two linked source-figures feeding a third (LOOPS BETWEEN SOURCES), and two merging light-streams cresting then dimming (A PEAK OF SYNERGY) — with a fourth roundel beside them, a macaque reaching toward a symbol with light-threads from brain to arm (THE REACHING MONKEY). These four converge back into the spine at a scribe measuring a small stack of scrolls against towering unread ones (NOT ENOUGH DATA), then a scroll-ribbon unrolling with bright and dim patches (MOMENT BY MOMENT), and finally at the foot a neuron-figure weighing patterned tokens on a scale (PATTERNS, NOT TOTALS). Marginal vine-and-leaf ornament fills empty corners sparingly; no words appear anywhere except the lettered titles beneath each roundel in careful capitals.

plates.title: Building the Lattice of Information
plates.prompt: Illuminated manuscript page, vertical 2:3, aged parchment, brown ink line, muted gold and blue washes, matching the hand of the overview page. A single vine-line descends through seven framed roundels. First, a merchant stacks two separate coin-piles that fail to match a larger pile beside them (PARTS DON'T ADD UP). Next, a target-neuron figure glows brighter than its two incoming piles, visibly combining them (MORE THAN THE SUM). Then two robed scholars at a lectern unroll a scroll marked with dividing lines, splitting one shape into smaller labeled shapes (THE ALGEBRAIC SPLIT). Next, an ornate cartouche redrawing FIGURE A — the oval with two overlapping circles and four shaded zones — resting open on a scribe's desk as though being studied (FOUR DISTINCT PIECES). Then a balance scale with three named weights on one side and a single hidden stone on the other, nearly tipping (ONE CHOICE, THREE FREE). Then a builder facing a tangled scaffold of crossing beams beside a simple two-plank bridge (MORE PARENTS, MORE TANGLE). Finally, a scholar holds up an illuminated lattice diagram — redrawing FIGURE B — its branching lines connecting small glowing jewel-nodes, a tree of information atoms (THE LATTICE OF ATOMS). Marginal vine-and-leaf ornament only in empty corners, never crowding the roundels. No lettering anywhere on the page except the titles in careful capitals beneath each roundel.

plates.title: What the Recordings Revealed
plates.prompt: Illuminated manuscript page, vertical 2:3, aged parchment, brown ink line, muted gold and blue washes, matching the hand of the earlier pages. A vine-line descends and briefly forks among seven framed roundels. At top, an illuminated panel redrawing FIGURE C: a sagittal brain slice resting on a fine electrode-grid, with small glowing triangular triads of three linked neurons picked out among the mass of points (THOUSANDS OF TRIADS). Below, a measuring rod held against a flowing stream of light, marking off a brighter quarter-length of it (A QUARTER OF THE FLOW). The line then forks into three roundels side by side: a richly adorned cluster of neuron-figures glowing far brighter than scattered plain ones (THE RICH CLUB'S SHARE); two source-figures bound by a looping cord glowing brighter than an unlooped pair (THE LOOP ADDS LIGHT); and a hill-shaped path of light rising to a single flagged peak then falling (A SINGLE PEAK). These three converge into one roundel showing a dish holding cultured tissue under glass, a whole living brain sketched faintly beyond its rim (CULTURE, NOT LIVING BRAIN). Finally at the foot, a reaching macaque's arm wrapped in many parallel duplicate threads of light running to its hand (REDUNDANCY IN THE REACH). Marginal vine-and-leaf ornament fills only empty corners sparingly. No lettering anywhere on the page except the titles in careful capitals beneath each roundel.

vignettes.quote: triads with two recurrent connections and no feedback connections had 50% more synergy
vignettes.depicts: Two source-figures bound by a looping cord between themselves glow half again as bright as a plain pair without the loop.
vignettes.title: THE LOOP ADDS LIGHT

vignettes.quote: the peak in synergy occurred when the mutual information was about 7% of the maximal value
vignettes.depicts: A hill-shaped path of light rising to a single marked peak and falling away on the far side, a small flag at the summit.
vignettes.title: A SINGLE PEAK

vignettes.quote: the processing we studied was in cortical cultures
vignettes.depicts: A dish holding a thin slice of cultured tissue under glass, set apart from a distant sketch of a whole living brain beyond the dish's rim.
vignettes.title: CULTURE, NOT LIVING BRAIN

vignettes.quote: the relative abundance of redundant information increased dramatically
vignettes.depicts: A reaching macaque's arm, around which many duplicate glowing threads run in parallel toward the hand, as if the same signal were sent many times over.
